top.title: Scientists check their work and confirm it with update on iconic black hole image
top.description: The image of the red ring around the black hole M87, produced by the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) array, made front-page news around the world in 2019. There was one problem: there was a slim chance the depiction might be wrong. This week, a small team of four Australian researchers have published their work confirming the result based on a new machine learning algorithm using the same base data. The 2019 Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) image came from hundreds of scientists working together to capture the first direct view of a black hole's shadow. The measurements were taken at eight telescopes around the world, at locations including Chile, the US, and Antarctica. Reconstructing the image from the data so geographically distant meant instrument and environment errors could influence the accuracy of the resulting image. Potentially, alternative analyses of the data could have reconstructed an image without the iconic ring shape. Samuel Lai – a postdoctoral fellow at the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO) in Western Australia – and his team created an independent imaging algorithm to process the historic dataset to validate the result. The new approach used closed triplets (using three telescopes for error correction) rather than station pairs in an effort to reduce error. To the relief of the EHT team, the new image recreated the iconic ring-like image seen in the original, according to a paper published in Nature today . In a prepared statement, Lai said taking pictures of black holes was not easy. "It is like standing in your backyard and trying to take a photo of a doughnut on the Moon," he said. He explained that when his team applied new advanced machine learning and artificial intelligence techniques to the original Event Horizon Telescope dataset, they found a black hole almost identical in size and shape to the historic EHT image. "Importantly, our model had no idea what a black hole looked like when we applied it to the M87 data. This is the first truly independent validation of the EHT image, an important step in the scientific process," he said. Event Horizon Telescope director Laurent Loinard welcomed the new study. "It is extremely gratifying to see that an elegant, entirely independent method recovers the ring structure of M87 across several years, in excellent agreement with the EHT Collaboration's published results," he said. ®

top.title: Did comets bring building blocks of life to Earth? Scientists aren't so sure anymore
top.description: The origin of life on Earth remains a mystery. New research shows that comets almost certainly did not bring the chemical building blocks of life to our planet. Life as we know it is based around carbon chemistry, also known as organic chemistry. Complex organic molecules are the fundamental building blocks of biochemical compounds such as nucleobases, amino acids, sugars and so on that act as the machinery for biochemistry on Earth . Two big questions are where did this complex chemistry originate? Did these complex organic molecules form on Earth, or were they delivered here from space? New research led by planetary scientist Richard Anslow of the Institute for Astronomy at the University of Cambridge has now seemingly ruled out comets as the origin of complex organic molecules on Earth. "Historically, scientists thought that comets were important for the origin of life on Earth, because they carried carbon and nitrogen-bearing molecules, so these giant space snowballs were almost like a 'get-out-of-jail-free card' that brought all the molecules a planet would need to seed life," said Anslow in a statement . Stripping the romance from the Earth's turbulent past Comet impacts on Earth were much more frequent in the first half-billion years of the solar system ’s existence, when there were still lots of debris leftover from the formation of the planets. For over a century comet impacts had been considered a prime suspect in the search for what brought the building blocks of life to Earth. However, while comets bringing the building blocks of life to Earth is "kind of a romantic idea," according to Anslow, the University of Cambridge researcher added that the team's results suggest that is highly unlikely. Anslow and colleagues arrived at this conclusion based upon computer modeling by using the very latest simulations depicting the origin and evolution of comets and their orbits, their interactions with Earth's atmosphere as they enter it, and of the hypervelocity comet impacts themselves. In particular, they used the fate of hydrogen cyanide as a proxy for what happens to complex organic molecules in comet impacts. Hydrogen cyanide is frequently found in comets and was even detected in the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS . An artist’s impression of a comet crashing into the early Earth (Image credit: Scarlett White) The problem is that comets are generally moving at too great a velocity. For organic molecules to survive impact, the impact velocity would have to be below 33,500 miles per hour (15 kilometers per second). Anslow and his colleagues found that, in general, comets travel too fast and enter Earth’s atmosphere at too sharp an angle for complex organic molecules to survive. Instead, they are mostly vaporized on impact. Even on the rare occasions that the complex organic molecules survived, they were usually not in great enough abundance to provide any meaningful prebiotic chemistry. top.description: By Peter Egwuatu The Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) has warned company directors against treating regulatory compliance as the sole responsibility of company secretaries, saying weak corporate records and governance failures could undermine business credibility, investment prospects and access to credit. Magaji said directors’ responsibilities extended beyond strategy, profitability and risk management to protecting the integrity of their companies’ legal identities. He noted that outdated corporate records, undisclosed changes in ownership and failure to file annual returns could expose companies to regulatory sanctions, reputational damage and diminished investor confidence. According to him, “Directors must demonstrate diligence, transparency and accountability by ensuring accurate corporate records, timely statutory filings and proper disclosure of persons with significant control. “The era of filing annual returns as an annual ritual is over. In simple terms, the Baja 1000 is a major off-road rally that takes place on Mexico’s Baja California peninsula (not in California, USA); while the exact route and distance change every year, competitors can expect to tackle over 800 miles of unforgiving desert silt, scrubland, and rocky mountain passes in pursuit of victory. The race itself is run all at once; drivers cross through several checkpoints along the way that capture their total elapsed time, and they can stop in makeshift pits to swap drivers—though driver swaps aren't necessary. The duration of the race depends on the length of the course and the class of vehicle. Top professionals in the top classes can finish shorter courses in as little as 15 hours, while slower vehicles on longer courses may take up to 50 hours to complete the race. The folks who take on the challenge do so in a variety of desert-equipped vehicles that comprise distinct classes, from top-of-the-line Trophy Trucks and vintage Volkswagen Beetles to UTVs and motorcycles. And it's the kind of race that welcomes all-comers, from pros supported by sponsors like Red Bull to competitors who rely on their family to serve as their pit crew. A Trophy Truck goes through tech at the 2024 Baja 1000. (Photo credit: Elizabeth Blackstock/FanAmp) While the race isn't as expansive as the Dakar Rally, where racers compete for thousands of miles over the course of several days, the Baja 1000 is just as fascinating when it comes to in-race action. And because the race's organizers, SCORE International, allow entries from all-comers, Baja is almost always packed to the brim with frankly unbelievable storylines. Today, we're taking a look at just five of them that illustrate how unpredictable, and captivating, the race can be. top.title: Mizzou soccer hires Paul Hart, Stanford AHC, as next head coach
top.description: Mizzou soccer has named its third head coach in program history. The Tigers announced Tuesday night that they have hired Stanford associated head coach Paul Hart to lead the Mizzou program beginning in the 2027 season. Hart will replace Stefanie Golan , who was the head coach in Columbia for the past six seasons. "I'm incredibly honored and excited to become the head coach at the University of Missouri ," Hart said in a news release. "Mizzou is a special place, with a tremendous university and a commitment to competing at the highest level. I'm grateful to Laird Veatch and Angie Jabir and everyone involved in this process. I'm eager to get to Columbia, build relationships with our student-athletes and begin the work of leading a program that our university and community will be proud to support. We have high expectations, and I'm excited about what we can accomplish together." According to the news release, Hart has agreed to a five-year contract with Missouri. The terms of that contract were not immediately available. Hart will remain with the Cardinal through the end of their season. Stanford finished the regular season with an 11-4-2 record and are expected to make the NCAA Tournament field, which will be announced Nov. 16. He worked under longtime Stanford head coach Paul Ratcliffe for the past six seasons. The Cardinal were the national runner-up in both 2023 and 2025 and made it to the Women’s College Cup semifinals in 2024. Hart is a London native who played college soccer at West Texas A&M, where he won the Lone Star Conference’s Goalkeeper of the Year honors for four straight years. He spent three years with Queens Park Rangers’ academy in England in the mid-1990s. Before joining Stanford, where he was promoted to associate head coach after the 2025 season, Hart spent time as an assistant coach and recruiting coordinator at Washington, Oklahoma and San Francisco. He began his coaching career as the goalkeepers coach at UC Santa Barbara. Hart will be the third head coach in program history. Golan, who Mizzou parted ways with earlier this month, had been the head coach for six years after taking over for Bryan Blitz, who had led the program since its inception. "He has played an integral role in building an elite, nationally recognized program at Stanford, recruiting and developing some of the best players in the country and competing for national championships. We believe he has the leadership and expertise to elevate our program, and we're excited to welcome Paul to Columbia as we pursue sustained success and compete for championships." nigeria.title: CAC, EY warn directors against governance failures
nigeria.description: By Peter Egwuatu The Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) has warned company directors against treating regulatory compliance as the sole responsibility of company secretaries, saying weak corporate records and governance failures could undermine business credibility, investment prospects and access to credit. He noted that outdated corporate records, undisclosed changes in ownership and failure to file annual returns could expose companies to regulatory sanctions, reputational damage and diminished investor confidence. nigeria.title: Apo-Karshi road to become Abuja tourist attraction – Wike
nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has said the Apo-Karshi road, a project awarded in 2010 but abandoned for years, will be developed into a tourist attraction in Abuja. Wike spoke on Wednesday during an inspection of the completed road in the nation’s capital. He attributed the completion of the project to President Bola Tinubu’s intervention, saying the President ordered the termination of the original contract after the contractor failed to deliver despite receiving full payment. “This road was awarded in 2010 to an indigenous contractor. We did all we could to persuade the contractor to ensure that the job was fully implemented, even though we had fully paid. But the contractor was not forthcoming,” he said. According to the minister, the matter was brought to Tinubu’s attention, following which the President directed that the contract be terminated and re-awarded to a more competent company. Wike said the decision was informed by the strategic importance of the road to residents and the overall development of the FCT. He added that the administration was not deterred by criticism over the cost of the new contract. “When this contract was awarded, some people were asking how we could award it at that amount. But we were not deterred. All we were concerned about was the happiness and comfort of the people,” he said. Wike described the road as one of the most publicised projects undertaken by the Satellite Towns Development Authority (STDA), noting that the difficult terrain made its completion a remarkable engineering achievement. He said reactions on social media showed that many Nigerians were surprised that a project of such scale and engineering complexity could be delivered in the country. The minister also acknowledged journalists for drawing public attention to the project, saying their reports had helped Nigerians appreciate the scale of work carried out on the road. He urged Nigerians to assess the Tinubu administration’s performance holistically rather than judging it based on isolated issues. “Look at what is going on in Abuja today, the level of infrastructure and how it has turned out to be a tourist centre. I am happy that people are happy and that Nigerians have seen the infrastructure development being carried out by the Tinubu administration,” he said. On the commissioning of the road, Wike said the FCT Administration was working around the President’s schedule, as several other projects were also being lined up for inauguration. He expressed hope that Tinubu would inaugurate the Apo-Karshi road before the end of November, adding that efforts would be made to secure a place for the project in the President’s schedule. On plans for public facilities around the road, the minister said the administration would develop appropriate amenities in collaboration with relevant departments. The resolution followed the adoption of a motion sponsored by Rep. Dominic Okafor, titled, “Need to Investigate the Alarming Increase in Human Trafficking in Nigeria”, at Wednesday’s plenary. The lawmakers expressed concern over the growing threat posed by human trafficking, particularly to women, children and other vulnerable groups. The House noted that human trafficking remained a grave violation of human rights and dignity, involving the recruitment, transportation, transfer, harbouring or receipt of persons through force, coercion, deception, abuse of vulnerability or other prohibited means for the purpose of exploitation. It observed that victims were increasingly subjected to commercial sexual exploitation, forced labour, domestic servitude, forced begging, organ harvesting and other forms of degrading abuse. The lawmakers attributed the growing vulnerability of Nigerians to trafficking to poverty, unemployment, insecurity, displacement, irregular migration and the activities of organised criminal networks. They further noted that many victims were lured through false promises of employment, education, marriage and opportunities abroad, only to end up in exploitative conditions characterised by physical abuse, psychological trauma and, in some cases, death. The House also expressed concern that trafficking networks operated across state and international borders, exploiting porous borders, inadequate public awareness, weak coordination among relevant agencies and difficulties in identifying and prosecuting offenders. While acknowledging the efforts of the National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP), the Nigeria Police Force, the Nigeria Immigration Service and other relevant institutions, the lawmakers stressed the need to strengthen their operational capacity, funding, intelligence-sharing and victim-support mechanisms. The House recalled the provisions of the Trafficking in Persons (Prohibition) Enforcement and Administration Act, 2015, and other relevant legislation aimed at preventing trafficking, prosecuting offenders and protecting victims. Consequently, the lawmakers urged the Federal Government to intensify nationwide efforts to combat human trafficking through effective enforcement of existing laws, intelligence-led investigations and prosecution of traffickers and their collaborators. nigeria.title: 2027: SDP inaugurates 12,000-member campaign council, names Tanko coordinator
nigeria.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election, the Social Democratic Party (SDP) has inaugurated a 12,000-member Presidential Campaign Council, PCC, with Dr Yunusa Tanko appointed as its National Coordinator. The SDP National Chairman, Professor Sadiq Gombe, who will also serve as chairman of the council, inaugurated the campaign council on Wednesday in Abuja. Gombe charged members of the council to work towards securing electoral victory for the party, stressing that its campaign must be issue-based, people-centred and guided by the provisions of the Constitution, the Electoral Act, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) guidelines and the party’s constitution. He urged members to approach the election with the seriousness it deserved, adding that the party was determined to challenge President Bola Tinubu at the polls. “Let us approach this election with the seriousness it deserves to unseat President Tinubu. “Our campaign must be issue-based, people-centred and firmly rooted in the provisions of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, the Electoral Act, INEC guidelines and our party constitution. “We must earn the confidence of Nigerians through credible engagement, persuasion, effective organisation and practical policy alternatives. “We must reject violence, intimidation, electoral malpractice and every conduct capable of undermining the integrity of our democracy,” he said. The SDP chairman described Nigeria as being at a critical crossroads, citing insecurity, economic hardship, unemployment, poverty, institutional weaknesses and declining public confidence in governance as some of the challenges confronting the country. According to him, Nigerians are yearning for purposeful leadership, economic opportunities, social justice, security and accountability, as well as a government that prioritises their welfare and dignity. He said the SDP was determined to provide Nigerians with a credible democratic alternative founded on social justice, equity, freedom, inclusive development and good governance. Gombe urged members of the campaign council to take the party’s message to communities across the country, engage citizens respectfully, listen to their concerns and demonstrate through their conduct that the party deserved their confidence. He further charged the council to ensure that the party’s campaign remained peaceful, credible and focused on offering practical solutions to the country’s challenges. nigeria.title: Manchester United ‘Reach Verbal Agreement’ With Ex-Chelsea Coach Pochettino To Replace Carrick
nigeria.description: Manchester United have reportedly reached a “verbal agreement in principle” with Argentine Mauricio Pochettino to replace embattled Michael Carrick as their manager in a bid to revive the fortunes of the struggling English giants. Carrick’s position at Old Trafford has been the subject of intense speculation following United’s worst start to a season in 40 years, leaving them languishing in the Premier League relegation zone after an eight-match winless run. He remains in post, but it is believed Carrick’s future will be decided at a meeting attended by influential shareholder Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox in Monaco on Wednesday. Berrada and Wilcox are reportedly leaning towards dismissing Carrick. United States head coach Pochettino has extensive experience of the Premier League following spells in charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. It was only three months ago, however, that Pochettino signed a contract extension to remain with the United States through to the 2030 World Cup. US Soccer would be due compensation should he move to Manchester, with the 54-year-old understood to have a $10 million (£7.5 million) release clause. But Sky Sports reported Wednesday that United have “reached a verbal agreement in principle” with Pochettino, linked with a move to Old Trafford on several previous occasions, to become their new head coach. Turbulent Reign Carrick was seen arriving at United’s Carrington training ground on Wednesday, but it appears to be only a matter of time before his turbulent reign comes to an end. Manchester United’s English head coach Michael Carrick reacts on the touchline during the English Premier League football match between Chelsea and Manchester United at Stamford Bridge in London on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Glyn KIRK / AFP) The 45-year-old had been granted a stay of execution after he was widely expected to be axed in late October following a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth. But United were beaten 2-0 at Chelsea, then scrambled a last-gasp 3-2 win against Roma in the Champions League after falling two goals down. It appeared former United and England midfielder Carrick would be on the way out when his team twice trailed Aston Villa by two goals on Sunday. When United scored twice in stoppage time to rescue an improbable 4-4 draw, it was interpreted as a positive sign for Carrick as the players were still fighting for him. But a change now appears likely, with former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe, ex-Chelsea chief Antonio Conte and former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann also linked with the United job. nigeria.description: President Bola Tinubu has received the Flamingos after winning Africa’s first-ever U-17 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Morocco. The First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, received the victorious players and technical crew on behalf of the President at the Presidential Banquet Hall, Abuja. ﻿ The U-17 team won their first FIFA World Cup title after defeating Japan 2-1 in the final on November 7, with goals from Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku securing the historic victory. The Flamingos lost their opener 2-1 to Poland, but dominated in the remaining matches, defeating defending champions North Korea, Puerto Rico, and Mexico. Their first-ever appearance in the final was sealed with a 3-1 victory over Brazil, before taking home the trophy after beating Japan. Flamingos celebrating their U-17 FIFA Women’s World Cup The players have received commendations from government officials and football fans around the world. President Tinubu congratulated the Flamingos for becoming the first African team to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Tinubu, in a statement by his spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, said he received the news upon his return from campaign engagements in Akwa Ibom and Rivers States. He also described Nigeria’s maiden triumph as a proud moment for the country and a landmark achievement for African women’s football. The Senate also pledged a ₦100 million reward for the Flamingos. The pledge followed a motion moved by the Chairman of the Senate Committee on Sports, Senator Abdul Ningi, who congratulated the players on their outstanding performance and commended the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) for its role in the team’s achievement. The latest feat by a Nigerian sports team came less than two years after the senior women’s football team, Super Falcons, won their 10th Women’s Africa Cup of Nations title in Morocco. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Russia’s Central Bank Clears Exchange to Open Bitcoin and Crypto Trading on Nov. 22 The Bank of Russia said Wednesday that exchanges may start organized trading in cryptocurrencies on Nov. 22, once the central bank has approved their trading rules, a step that lands just ahead of Moscow Exchange’s planned Dec. 1 bitcoin launch. The ordinance, which amends the Bank of Russia’s rules for organized trading, was registered by the Justice Ministry on Nov. 3 and published Wednesday on the regulator’s site. It takes effect 10 days after publication, on Nov. 22. Exchanges will have to register the brokers, trust managers and central counterparties that take part in crypto trades, keep registers of orders and deals, and monitor the activity. They must also calculate a current price, a weighted-average price, a market price and a closing price, and report trading activity to the central bank in the same way they already do for other assets. The regulator was clear about the order of operations. Exchanges may open crypto markets from Nov. 22, it said, “but first they must agree with the regulator on the rules for conducting such trading.” It did not say whether any venue has already cleared that review. Who can buy, and what they can buy A separate ordinance, published Nov. 6 and due to take effect Nov. 17, sets the menu for ordinary buyers. The Bank of Russia approved bitcoin, ether and Tether’s USDT for purchase by non-qualified investors, and said exchanges may admit those assets to public trading from that date. Non-qualified investors can buy through a broker, a trust manager or a registered crypto exchange office, on an exchange or over the counter. Purchases through a single intermediary may not exceed 300,000 rubles a year, roughly $3,600 at the official exchange rate. Qualified investors can access all cryptoassets with no purchase cap. Both groups still have to pass a knowledge test and read a risk disclosure before they can trade. The list is limited to the most liquid assets that meet the law’s tests for market capitalization, average daily volume and at least five years of pricing history on foreign exchanges. Moscow Exchange still aims for Dec. 1 Moscow Exchange, Russia’s largest trading venue, announced on Nov. 2 that it plans to offer bitcoin, ether and USDT trades from Dec. 1, initially as a pilot while participants connect. Trading would run on its existing stock-market systems from 6:50 a.m. to 11:50 p.m. Moscow time, with the National Clearing Centre clearing the deals and clients able to settle the same day or the next. Bitcoin Magazine reported the Dec. 1 plan last week, including the U.S. sanctions that already cover the exchange and its clearing house. business.title: ICE and OKX Set Nov. 23 Tokenized Stock Launch After 67 Companies Opt Out
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine ICE and OKX Set Nov. 23 Tokenized Stock Launch After 67 Companies Opt Out OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) will open their tokenized stock venue on Nov. 23, the companies said Wednesday, offering more than 70 assets under a temporary SEC exemption even as 67 companies, including Apple, Tesla and Meta, have already objected. The OKX announcement said more than 70 assets are expected to be listed, including securities from Better.com, BitGo, Circle, Coinbase, Robinhood, Securitize and Strategy (MSTR), as well as 59 exchange-traded funds from Direxion. Strategy will also list its preferred stocks, such as STRC. Access at launch is limited to eligible U.S. customers of OKX Inc. who have activated a CeDeFi Wallet, passed identity checks and completed onboarding with the joint venture, which is called OKXICE and is owned equally by ICE and OKC USA Holding Inc., an OKX affiliate. Trading will run around the clock in the OKX app. “The future of finance is onchain, and we have an opportunity to build it here in America, with the standards, safeguards and ambition that investors expect,” said former New York Gov. Andrew Cuomo, who co-chairs OKXICE with Trabue Bland. The companies did not say how many of the more than 70 assets will trade on the first day, or how much liquidity the pools will have at the open. The venue is not a registered exchange or broker-dealer and is not approved by the SEC, the announcement said. How the venue will work Trading will run through automated market maker pools built on Uniswap v4 and deployed on X Layer, the Ethereum layer-2 network OKX operates. Only approved wallets can trade or add liquidity. Securitize will provide the tokenization infrastructure. Each token represents a security entitlement backed one-for-one by a U.S. share held by a registered broker-dealer, and holders keep the usual shareholder rights, including dividends, voting and corporate actions, the venue said in a Nov. 5 public notice required under the exemption. Customers will hold the tokens in their own wallets. OKXICE will not hold the assets or the private keys. The tokens will be paired with payment stablecoins such as USDC and USDG. The venue does not operate an order book, does not extend credit and does not conduct primary offerings, the notice said. 67 companies have already opted out The same Nov. 5 notice lists 67 issuers that had sent a written objection by that date, among them Apple, Amazon, Tesla, Meta, Netflix, Nvidia, Microsoft, JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Costco, Nike and Home Depot. The list has grown from 50 objectors in an Oct. 30 notice. The objections stem from the SEC’s five-year “Innovation Exemption,” issued Sept. 17, which lets tokenized securities venues trade blockchain versions of U.S. stocks through automated market makers without registering as exchanges. business.title: Deutsche Bank Switches On Bitcoin Custody for Paying Clients
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Deutsche Bank Switches On Bitcoin Custody for Paying Clients Deutsche Bank has switched on its digital asset custody service for paying clients, the German lender said Wednesday, letting institutions and corporations in Europe hold bitcoin with the country’s largest bank less than two months after it first unveiled the plan. The bank announced the service on Sept. 16, saying it would go live with first clients this year once regulators signed off. It now supports bitcoin and ether, along with the USDC, EURC and EURAU stablecoins, according to its product page . Under the setup, Deutsche Bank manages the wallets and private keys on behalf of clients, who can store the assets and transfer them to third parties. The bank pitched that as a way for clients to skip building and maintaining their own custody infrastructure. “In the medium term we aim to deliver a fully integrated, regulated ecosystem that supports the custody, tokenisation, and settlement of digital assets,” said Paul Maley, global head of trust and securities services at Deutsche Bank. The bank did not name its first clients, say how many have signed up or disclose what it charges to hold the coins. The service is aimed at institutional and corporate clients, not retail customers. What Deutsche Bank is offering The product page describes private keys stored in hardware security modules, a choice of warm and cold storage, multi-factor authentication, segregation of client assets and a customizable approval process for client transfers. Clients reach the service through Autobahn, Deutsche Bank’s multi-channel gateway, or its Corporate Bank portal. The service is booked out of Deutsche Bank AG in Frankfurt and is available in Germany, with cross-border servicing across Europe through passporting. The bank lists institutional investors, multinationals and corporates, governments and sovereigns, and wealth managers as target clients, and it describes the offering as compliant with the European Union’s MiCA crypto rules. For now the menu is narrow. Deutsche lists custody, transfers and internal moves between warm and cold storage as its initial services, with “further capabilities planned.” The September release said the asset list may grow with client demand and that tokenized financial instruments are on the roadmap. It also carried a warning familiar to anyone in bitcoin: crypto assets held this way are not covered by a deposit-guarantee scheme like the one that protects eligible bank deposits. A tie-up with Deutsche Asset Management Alongside the launch, Deutsche Bank signed a memorandum of understanding with Deutsche Asset Management, the money manager it mostly owns that was known until recently as DWS. The agreement is meant “to explore comprehensive commercial and technical collaboration opportunities in the digital asset space,” the bank said. entertainment.title: What Are The Effective Ways of Using AI?
entertainment.description: Two people engaging with technology in a contemporary hotel lobby work setting. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is changing how people learn, work, communicate and solve problems. In today’s world, if you’re not on board with AI, it could be said you’re being resistant to the fastest-growing technological innovation in the world. From students researching academic subjects to professionals developing business ideas, AI tools have become companions in everyday activities for people. They can help save time, explore new ideas, understand difficult concepts and approach tasks differently. However, as more people embrace these AI tools, it is important to understand that using AI effectively goes beyond knowing what prompts to enter. It requires knowing when to use it, how to question its responses and, most importantly, when to rely on your own knowledge and judgement. AI could make us better at what we do, not make us dependent on it. Here are ways we think you use AI effectively: Use AI as a Research Assistant One of the most effective ways to use AI is for research and information gathering. Whether you are writing an article, preparing a presentation or exploring an unfamiliar subject, AI can help you identify relevant topics, explain complex ideas and suggest areas worth investigating. You can ask it to break down unfamiliar concepts, identify key questions, or suggest research directions. However, do not treat every response as fact. Verify important information using credible sources, published research, books and reliable websites. AI can help you find information, but you are responsible for establishing what is true. Use AI to Brainstorm and Explore Ideas Like knowledge gathering, AI can brainstorm ideas with you. Sometimes, the hardest part of starting a project is knowing where to begin. AI can help you overcome this challenge by suggesting ideas, exploring different approaches and presenting perspectives you may not have considered. For writers, entrepreneurs, researchers and creatives, it can be a useful brainstorming partner. You can share an idea, ask questions about its strengths and weaknesses, and explore ways to develop it. However, brainstorming should not become an excuse to surrender your imagination. Let AI expand your thinking, not replace it. Use AI to Improve Your Work, Not Replace Your Skills This is becoming more important. AI can help you identify grammatical errors, improve sentence construction, organise information, summarise lengthy documents and make your communication clearer. It can reduce the time spent on repetitive tasks and create more room for important responsibilities. The important thing is that you should remain actively involved. entertainment.title: 5 New Albums to Listen to This Week: Skepta, Phyno, Ty Bello & More
entertainment.description: Skepta holding the official clear vinyl edition of his sixth studio album, The Fork and Knife. Photo Credit: Skepta/Instagram Your playlist could do with a little shake-up, and these five albums might be exactly what it needs. Skepta is reconnecting with his roots, Phyno is giving us more of the indigenous rap we love, Ty Bello has two albums exploring different expressions of worship, and Anendlessocean and Tobe Nwigwe are taking their sounds in interesting directions. From UK grime and Nigerian hip-hop to alternative gospel and soul, there’s a lot to discover across these new releases. Whether you’re in the mood for bars, worship, thoughtful songwriting or music that brings different cultures together, this week’s selection has something worth hearing. Skepta: The Fork & Knife Back in 2012, Skepta found himself at odds with a corporatised grime scene, sparking a pivotal career reckoning that eventually led to his landmark 2016 album Konnichiwa. On his long-awaited 15-track sixth album, The Fork & Knife, the 44-year-old MC reflects on his journey as grime’s most influential elder statesman and the son of Nigerian immigrants. Named after his mother’s favourite proverb, the record is a deep exploration of identity and perseverance. Musically, Skepta bridges continents by blending global diasporic sounds. He teams up with Aya Nakamura on the zouk-infused “ Chippie ”, taps Asake for the Afrobeats crossover “ Aloe Vera ”, and recruits Chase & Status alongside Suggs for the sharp single “ Innocent Smile ”. The project closes with “ Belly ”, an eight-minute masterclass featuring Boy Better Know members Jme and Frisco . ﻿ Phyno: Let That Sink In Arriving nearly 10 years after his groundbreaking sophomore record The Playmaker, Phyno’s 15-track sixth solo album, Let That Sink In (LTSI), showcases his timeless command of indigenous rap. sports.description: Mizzou soccer has named its third head coach in program history. The Tigers announced Tuesday night that they have hired Stanford associated head coach Paul Hart to lead the Mizzou program beginning in the 2027 season. Hart will replace Stefanie Golan , who was the head coach in Columbia for the past six seasons. "I'm incredibly honored and excited to become the head coach at the University of Missouri ," Hart said in a news release. "Mizzou is a special place, with a tremendous university and a commitment to competing at the highest level. I'm grateful to Laird Veatch and Angie Jabir and everyone involved in this process. I'm eager to get to Columbia, build relationships with our student-athletes and begin the work of leading a program that our university and community will be proud to support. We have high expectations, and I'm excited about what we can accomplish together." According to the news release, Hart has agreed to a five-year contract with Missouri. The terms of that contract were not immediately available. Hart will remain with the Cardinal through the end of their season. Stanford finished the regular season with an 11-4-2 record and are expected to make the NCAA Tournament field, which will be announced Nov. 16. He worked under longtime Stanford head coach Paul Ratcliffe for the past six seasons. The Cardinal were the national runner-up in both 2023 and 2025 and made it to the Women’s College Cup semifinals in 2024. Hart is a London native who played college soccer at West Texas A&M, where he won the Lone Star Conference’s Goalkeeper of the Year honors for four straight years. He spent three years with Queens Park Rangers’ academy in England in the mid-1990s. Before joining Stanford, where he was promoted to associate head coach after the 2025 season, Hart spent time as an assistant coach and recruiting coordinator at Washington, Oklahoma and San Francisco. He began his coaching career as the goalkeepers coach at UC Santa Barbara. Hart will be the third head coach in program history. Golan, who Mizzou parted ways with earlier this month, had been the head coach for six years after taking over for Bryan Blitz, who had led the program since its inception. The Brewers received a compensation pick for Adames , while the shortstop went to San Francisco on a massive 7-year, $177 million deal. sports.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. sports.title: Ceará bid to avoid unprecedented relegation as 2025 scenario repeats
sports.description: Ceará bid to avoid unprecedented relegation as 2025 scenario repeats Ceará went into the 35th round of last year's Brasileirão with 42 points. They needed just three more to avoid relegation, with 12 still available. But they picked up only one against the four teams then in the top four (Mirassol, Cruzeiro, Flamengo and Palmeiras) and ended up relegated. They spent only the final half-hour of the season in the relegation zone, but that was enough to seal an unlikely drop. Now the situation for the black-and-white side from Porangabuçu is even more dramatic. Their mission against CRB next Saturday (14) is to avoid something unprecedented: relegation to Brazil's Série C. Favorites failed to deliver... Ceará actually made a positive start to the current Série B campaign, sitting sixth after six rounds and still unbeaten. It suggested they would challenge for an automatic promotion spot to Série A, or at least a place in the playoffs. That would have justified having one of the four biggest wage bills in the competition. Instead, they entered the closing stages battling relegation. They did rally, taking 11 of a possible 15 points between rounds 28 and 32 to move closer to safety. But then they got themselves into trouble: one draw and four defeats. Last Sunday's (8) defeat at home at Castelão to already-relegated América Mineiro also prompted coach Daniel Paulista to resign. And it left Vozão in a precarious position. The risk was just 1%... Before facing América Mineiro, Ceará were still in a comfortable position. They had lost to Athletic, but needed just one point from the remaining six to turn their attention fully to 2027. At that point, their mathematical chance of relegation was 1%, according to the Mathematics Department at the Federal University of Minas Gerais (UFMG). But defeat to another team from Minas Gerais left them in their current predicament. Their fate is still in their own hands, but the risk of relegation stands at 19.3%, and the situation is far from straightforward. They need at least a point against CRB at Rei Pelé to avoid a first-ever drop to the third tier. They have 43 points and 11 wins, sitting in 16th place. Avaí are just behind them on 40 points, with the same number of wins. The catch is that Vozão will be away to the team currently in sixth, who also have their fate in their own hands as they look to secure the final playoff spot. Avaí, meanwhile, will face Ceará's latest conquerors in Belo Horizonte. A defeat to CRB combined with an Avaí win would relegate Ceará. technology.title: Scientists check their work and confirm it with update on iconic black hole image
technology.description: The image of the red ring around the black hole M87, produced by the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) array, made front-page news around the world in 2019. There was one problem: there was a slim chance the depiction might be wrong. This week, a small team of four Australian researchers have published their work confirming the result based on a new machine learning algorithm using the same base data. The 2019 Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) image came from hundreds of scientists working together to capture the first direct view of a black hole's shadow. The measurements were taken at eight telescopes around the world, at locations including Chile, the US, and Antarctica. Reconstructing the image from the data so geographically distant meant instrument and environment errors could influence the accuracy of the resulting image. Potentially, alternative analyses of the data could have reconstructed an image without the iconic ring shape. Samuel Lai – a postdoctoral fellow at the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO) in Western Australia – and his team created an independent imaging algorithm to process the historic dataset to validate the result. The new approach used closed triplets (using three telescopes for error correction) rather than station pairs in an effort to reduce error. To the relief of the EHT team, the new image recreated the iconic ring-like image seen in the original, according to a paper published in Nature today . In a prepared statement, Lai said taking pictures of black holes was not easy. "It is like standing in your backyard and trying to take a photo of a doughnut on the Moon," he said. He explained that when his team applied new advanced machine learning and artificial intelligence techniques to the original Event Horizon Telescope dataset, they found a black hole almost identical in size and shape to the historic EHT image. "Importantly, our model had no idea what a black hole looked like when we applied it to the M87 data. This is the first truly independent validation of the EHT image, an important step in the scientific process," he said. Event Horizon Telescope director Laurent Loinard welcomed the new study. "It is extremely gratifying to see that an elegant, entirely independent method recovers the ring structure of M87 across several years, in excellent agreement with the EHT Collaboration's published results," he said. ®

Others say they received a 0x800F0989 error. Microsoft does not currently list any known issues with the update and is yet to make a statement or provide explanation for the glitch. In addition to the security fixes, this patch resolves a number of known issues from previous updates, including a problem where USB Audio 1.0 devices might fail to start and display an error code 10 in Device Manager. In the absence of a statement from Microsoft, several users have taken to sleuthing. One, with the handle of Forceflow on the ElevenForum site, suggested the bug might be related to Windows Sandbox, and said that after disabling the feature and rebooting, the patch installed successfully. However, others reported problems regardless of Windows Sandbox status, and alternative solutions included using DISM (Deployment Image Servicing and Management) to check the package or downloading the update manually. It's an important patch to install, since it addresses 726 vulnerabilities in Windows alone, and the difficulties affected users face are less than ideal. Microsoft patches have lately displayed more gremlins than usual. Out-of-band releases are depressingly regular after updates break functionality. A September Out-of-band release, for example, was hurriedly pushed out after the September 2026 Windows security update caused trouble for Remote Desktop Services. The October Patch Tuesday for Windows Server sent Exchange Servers toppling , with a registry edit workaround suggested. There was no out-of-band update - Microsoft said the problem had been resolved in the November update. At least this latest release appears to be failing before users get a chance to see what is broken this time. The Register has asked Microsoft to comment. ®

technology.title: NASA asks Earthlings to wave as Voyager 1 reaches a light-day away
technology.description: Voyager 1 will become the first human-made object to reach one light-day from Earth next week, and NASA wants us to mark the occasion by flashing our lights at the sky. The spacecraft, which suffered a communications hiccup last month, is traveling at approximately 38,000 mph (61,000 kph) and will mark the 50th anniversary of its launch next year. Before then, it has another distance record to set. "Light-day" is a bit snappier than 16,094,799,096 miles (25,902,068,356 kilometers). NASA puts the crossing at 05:16:07 EST (10:16:07 UTC) on Wednesday, November 18. For "Shine Bright for Voyager's Light-Day," participants are invited to flash the mission's three-letter designation – VGR – in Morse code after sunset on November 17, using a flashlight or NASA's website. According to the space agency, this will create "a symbolic wave of golden light encircling the planet after sunset." It is also a nice way to mark the achievement – Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object from Earth, and its extraordinary longevity remains a testament to the skill of engineers past and present. Not that Voyager 1 will be able to detect any flashlights on Earth. Its cameras were turned off decades ago, after the famous Pale Blue Dot image was captured. NASA has invited the public to join in a spacecraft photo opportunity before. On July 19, 2013, Cassini photographed Earth and the Moon from its orbit around Saturn for "The Day the Earth Smiled," while people back home were encouraged to look up and "just smile at the sheer joy of being alive on a Pale Blue Dot." Voyager 2, the spacecraft's sibling, is not expected to reach the same milestone for another nine years. It took a different path through the solar system to swing past Uranus and Neptune. It will, however, be uncertain as to whether Voyager 2 will still be able to communicate by then – even with recent efforts to eke out the probe's dwindling power supply, margins are razor thin. ®

It serves as further independent validation of the cryptography that protects massive quantities of the world's communications on platforms like the Signal app , Google Messages, and WhatsApp. And it demonstrates Google DeepMind's formal verification capabilities using a new AI framework called AlphaProof Code. More broadly, AI-aided formal verification is having a moment, but it is unclear how practical it will be for widespread use and how effective it can be at securing large amounts of code. Proponents of formal verification have long referred to it as a sort of holy grail in software security, because it uses math to check and validate that software is functioning as intended—in other words, that it doesn't have critical vulnerabilities. technology.title: 2013 breach at Russian cybercrime forum resurfaces with millions of victims' credentials
technology.description: A 2013 breach of Russian-language cybercrime forum YouHack exposed its members' login details – and millions of credentials they had posted about other victims, according to newly cataloged data. Have I Been Pwned (HIBP) added the breach on Wednesday, recording 7.2 million unique email addresses. Around 107,000 belonged to forum members, whose exposed data included usernames, IP addresses, and mostly unsalted MD5 password hashes. Unsalted MD5 is a poor choice for protecting passwords. It's fast to compute, allowing attackers to test guesses at speed, and identical passwords produce identical hashes. Hardly good hygiene for a hacking forum. You might expect members of a cybercrime forum to know better than to reuse passwords or register with an email address tied to their real identity. Expectations and reality are not always on speaking terms, as AlphaBay founder Alexandre Cazes demonstrated. YouHack, a longtime cybercrime forum, moved to a different domain after the 2013 breach and remains active, giving cybercrims a place to trade stolen credentials and financial data. The data collated from that digital burglary was eventually bundled into 2024's so-called Mother of all Breaches – a 12TB, 26 billion-record mega-dump of files taken from myriad data security lapses. Millions more HIBP separately published its findings concerning another Russian data breach today. It said the 2023 breach of Russian bank Sberbank's loyalty program (SberSpasibo) contained records belonging to 48 million users. The dataset included 3.3 million unique email addresses, alongside phone numbers and dates of birth. Bank card numbers were stored as unsalted SHA-1 hashes, which could let attackers test possible numbers against the leaked hashes for a match. Reporting on the SberSpasibo breach at the time suggested the records were dated between April 2017 and February 2022, and the attack was claimed by the pro-Ukraine hacktivist outfit NLB. NLB also claimed responsibility for an attack on Sberbank's internal systems at the same time, and later took partial credit for an attack on Alfa-Bank , Russia's largest private bank. ®

science.title: Did comets bring building blocks of life to Earth? Scientists aren't so sure anymore
science.description: The origin of life on Earth remains a mystery. New research shows that comets almost certainly did not bring the chemical building blocks of life to our planet. Life as we know it is based around carbon chemistry, also known as organic chemistry. Complex organic molecules are the fundamental building blocks of biochemical compounds such as nucleobases, amino acids, sugars and so on that act as the machinery for biochemistry on Earth . Two big questions are where did this complex chemistry originate? Did these complex organic molecules form on Earth, or were they delivered here from space? New research led by planetary scientist Richard Anslow of the Institute for Astronomy at the University of Cambridge has now seemingly ruled out comets as the origin of complex organic molecules on Earth. "Historically, scientists thought that comets were important for the origin of life on Earth, because they carried carbon and nitrogen-bearing molecules, so these giant space snowballs were almost like a 'get-out-of-jail-free card' that brought all the molecules a planet would need to seed life," said Anslow in a statement . Stripping the romance from the Earth's turbulent past Comet impacts on Earth were much more frequent in the first half-billion years of the solar system ’s existence, when there were still lots of debris leftover from the formation of the planets. For over a century comet impacts had been considered a prime suspect in the search for what brought the building blocks of life to Earth. However, while comets bringing the building blocks of life to Earth is "kind of a romantic idea," according to Anslow, the University of Cambridge researcher added that the team's results suggest that is highly unlikely. Anslow and colleagues arrived at this conclusion based upon computer modeling by using the very latest simulations depicting the origin and evolution of comets and their orbits, their interactions with Earth's atmosphere as they enter it, and of the hypervelocity comet impacts themselves. In particular, they used the fate of hydrogen cyanide as a proxy for what happens to complex organic molecules in comet impacts. Hydrogen cyanide is frequently found in comets and was even detected in the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS . An artist’s impression of a comet crashing into the early Earth (Image credit: Scarlett White) The problem is that comets are generally moving at too great a velocity. For organic molecules to survive impact, the impact velocity would have to be below 33,500 miles per hour (15 kilometers per second). Anslow and his colleagues found that, in general, comets travel too fast and enter Earth’s atmosphere at too sharp an angle for complex organic molecules to survive. Instead, they are mostly vaporized on impact. Even on the rare occasions that the complex organic molecules survived, they were usually not in great enough abundance to provide any meaningful prebiotic chemistry. science.title: Re-analysis of black hole data proves iconic ring shape really is there
science.description: The original black hole image (left) and the new image (right) S. Lai, N. Thyagarajan, O. I. Wong, and F. Diakogiannis; Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation/EHT collaboration When the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) team released their first image of a black hole in 2019, the astrophysics community was abuzz: the image of black hole M87* showed a perfect ring structure, just as predicted by the theory of general relativity. As other teams reanalysed the data in the following years, though, scepticism about the image began to slip in. A new, completely independent analysis has now finally banished that scepticism. The now-iconic doughnut shape of the EHT image is caused by a key property of general relativity, the way that light bends in the presence of an extremely massive object. Observing it for real was one of the strongest pieces of evidence that general relativity is accurate. Read more Hubble Space Telescope is falling to Earth – should NASA save it? What allowed us to finally capture the image was the unique structure of the EHT, which is made up of a network of telescopes all around the world, used as one Earth-sized radio dish. This allows it to peer much closer to the edge of a black hole than any other observatory. However, the same structure that enabled the image also limits the EHT. “It has only a handful of telescopes spread across the globe, which leaves large gaps in its measurements that the imaging algorithm has to fill in,” says Nithyanandan Thyagarajan at CSIRO in Australia. “It also observes at very short radio wavelengths, where the atmosphere can distort the signal.” Advertisement These limitations mean that the raw data from the EHT is more subject to interpretation than most astronomical observations, and the way the data is processed is particularly impactful on the final image. Most of the analyses of the M87* data produced similar ring shapes, but one that was published in 2022 found no ring at all. So, when Thyagarajan and his colleagues reanalysed the data, they developed an entirely new data pipeline to do so. Instead of analysing the data from pairs of EHT telescopes before combining them, which is the standard method, they grouped the telescopes into triplets. Free newsletter Sign up to Launchpad Sign up to newsletter “By combining measurements from sets of three telescopes, we preserve the information about the object’s shape while cancelling out errors from the atmosphere and the telescopes,” says Thyagarajan. They also developed a machine learning algorithm trained on non-black-hole images to minimise bias from their own expectations of what the image might look like. In the end, their new image is nearly identical to the original. This is a key confirmation of the EHT’s finding that general relativity truly does describe the space-time around a black hole accurately. Journal Reference: Nature DOI: 10.1038/s41586-026-11241-9

The 59-foot-tall (18 meters) expendable rocket and can haul 660 pounds (300 kilograms) to low Earth orbit (LEO). Neutron is the company's entry into the medium-lift market. It features a reusable first stage, stands 141 feet (43 m) tall and can carry 14.3 tons (13 metric tons) of payload to LEO. Rocket Lab announced Neutron back in 2021 and first targeted a 2024 debut for the vehicle. But various problems have cropped up over the years, pushing things back. Last month, for example, Rocket Lab announced that it was delaying the first Neutron flight from late 2026 into 2027 due to a manufacturing issue (which it says is now under control). science.description: null The Hubble Space Telescope has captured a breathtaking view of thousands of stars glittering like cosmic jewels in a dazzling display of blue, gold and orange. But this spectacular scene is far more than just a pretty picture. Some of these stars are almost as old as the universe itself and could hold clues to how our Milky Way formed. M30 is a globular star cluster located approximately 27,500 light-years from Earth. (Image credit: ESA/Hubble & NASA, M. Libralato, G. Piotto, A. Sarajedini) What is it? The exquisite image released by ESA on Nov. 5 shows Messier 30 (M30), a densely packed collection of stars located approximately 27,500 light-years from Earth in the constellation Capricornus. M30 is a globular cluster, a roughly spherical collection of tens of thousands to millions of stars held together by gravity . Our Milky Way is home to at least 150 of these ancient stellar gatherings, some of which are estimated to be between 11.5 billion and 13.5 billion years old. For comparison, the universe itself is approximately 13.8 billion years old! Why is it amazing Besides looking like a vast cosmic treasure trove glittering across the universe, M30 also has a fascinating story to tell. Globular clusters are essentially cosmic time capsules. Their ancient stars preserve chemical clues about the conditions that existed when they formed, helping astronomers piece together the Milky Way's early history. Astronomers have also discovered that M30, along with several other globular clusters, traverses the Milky Way in the opposite direction to the galaxy's rotation. This unusual motion raises the intriguing possibility that M30 may not have formed in our galaxy at all. It could have simply been captured by the Milky Way billions of years ago.

Thus, when it launches in 2031, UVEX will join new sky-mapping surveys like NASA's SPHEREx (Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer), which scans the cosmos in infrared, and the Vera C. UVEX's ultraviolet views will reveal explosive events such as the collisions between ultra-dense stellar corpses called neutron stars and the supernova explosions that mark the deaths of massive stars and the births of neutron stars and black holes. Additionally, the NASA ultraviolet telescope should be able to detect a multitude of low-mass galaxies much closer to the Milky Way than similar galaxies that are currently being observed millions and even billions of light-years away by NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) . The $590 million UVEX mission will "advance fundamental frontiers in astrophysics, from understanding the smallest galaxies to diagnosing the aftermath of neutron-star mergers and other cosmic explosions," the mission's principal investigator, Caltech physics professor Fiona Harrison, said in an Oct. 27 statement . science.description: null SpaceX is one big step closer to the 15th test flight of its Starship megarocket. The company announced today (Nov. 10) that it had moved its latest Starship first stage, known as Super Heavy Booster 22, to the launch mount at its Starbase facility in South Texas ahead of Flight 15, which is scheduled to lift off this Friday (Nov. 13). During the upcoming launch test, SpaceX plans to catch both Booster 22 and Starship's Ship upper stage with its launch tower's "chopstick" arms in a double landing catch — something the private spaceflight company has never tried before. It will be the first full recovery of an orbital rocket in history. SpaceX's Flight 15 Starship Super Heavy booster in its assembly bay, before its move to Starbase's launch mount. (Image credit: SpaceX) Booster 22 therefore "was used for final catch testing upon arrival [at the pad], including a suspended squeeze test at catch height," SpaceX said in an X post today (Nov. 10). That post shared four photos of the giant booster, which is powered by 33 of SpaceX's next-gen Raptor engines. The first shot showed Super Heavy in one of Starbase's "Mega Bay" assembly buildings before rollout, while the other three depicted it grasped by the tower's arms, held high in the South Texas sky. SpaceX will try to catch both Super Heavy and Ship during Flight 15 — something it's never done before. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX has used the chopstick arms during Starship flights before; it has successfully caught Super Heavy on three separate occasions. But the company has never attempted a catch of Ship, which flies higher and farther than the booster and is therefore a more challenging target. And SpaceX only reached orbit with Starship for the first time on Flight 14, which launched on Sept. 28. So Flight 15 will break new ground. And, if all goes to plan, it will give us a look at the future: SpaceX plans to catch Super Heavy and Ship on all operational Starship missions, as this recovery strategy will allow the company to boost the megarocket's launch cadence. And SpaceX wants to fly Starship incredibly often, so that it can build out its Starlink V3 broadband constellation and even bigger Starmind AI data-center network . Indeed, Elon Musk has said the company is eyeing 10,000 Starship flights per year by 2030. The launch tower's "chopstick" arms giving the Flight 15 Super Heavy a loving squeeze. (Image credit: SpaceX) If all goes to plan, Flight 15 will launch from Starbase on Friday during a 75-minute window that opens at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT; 4:45 p.m. local Texas time). Super Heavy will return to Starbase for its catch about 6.5 minutes after liftoff. Ship will follow suit much later — about 22 hours later, in fact, after it has deployed 26 Starlink V3 spacecraft into LEO and completed 14 circuits of our planet. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 10, 2013: Europe's GOCE satellite, the 'Ferrari of space,' fell out of orbit after mapping Earth's gravity field
science.description: null On Nov. 10, 2013, Europe's GOCE satellite fell to Earth after four years in orbit mapping the planet's gravitational field. GOCE, its name was short for Gravity field and steady-state Ocean Circulation Explorer, launched in 2009 on a mission to map Earth's gravity like never before. But despite that successful mission, it was doomed in 2013 when it ran out of fuel . At the time, controllers weren't sure where GOCE would fall back to Earth . Some people worried that it might crash into a populated area. However, the small spacecraft broke up in the atmosphere and didn't cause any property damage. It disintegrated about 50 miles above the Falkland Islands in the South Atlantic Ocean. The European Space Agency called the mission a success. GOCE lasted far longer than expected. It showed small variations in Earth's gravity , mapped the structure of Earth's crust and mantle, and tracked ocean currents. Artist's rendering of the "Ferrari of space," the European Space Agency's Gravity field and steady-state Ocean Circulation Explorer (GOCE), before it fell from space in 2013. (Image credit: European Space Agency) Why it mattered The GOCE satellite was a sleek spacecraft, with fins covered in solar panels that gave it a futuristic design. In fact, its look earned it a pretty cool nickname. "GOCE's sleek, elegant aerodynamic design — responsible for it being dubbed the 'Ferrari of space' — immediately set it apart from most other satellites,." ESA officials said in a description . There was more than looks behind GOCE's design. In order to generate the best map ever of Earth's gravitational field, GOCE had to fly in an orbit so low — just 139 miles (224 kilometers) — it needed to counteract the drag from the gossamer thin atmosphere of Earth at that altitude. The International Space Station orbits Earth at nearly twice that altitude. GOCE was powered by an xenon ion engine that allowed to maintain its low orbit for four years. Once it ran out of fuel, the 1-ton satellite could not maintain its position in space , leading to a fiery plunge to Earth. The large size of GOCE — it weighed 2,425 pounds (1,100 kilograms) and was 17 feet (5.3 meters) long and 3.2 feet (1 m) wide — made its reentry stand out, particularly since at least 25% of the satellite was expected to reach the Earth's surface . science.title: A distant exoplanet mysteriously vanished from sight. Astronomers just discovered why
science.description: null Astronomers have solved the mystery of an extrasolar planet, or exoplanet, that "disappeared" after seven years of observations. New research suggests that the planet hasn't vanished at all, but has been dragged off its orbit by an unseen planet. The exoplanet , designated TOI-2535 b, is located around 1,000 light-years away. TOI-2535 b was routinely observed with NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite ( TESS ) space telescope for seven years between April 2019 and March 2026 as it completed its 8.25-Earth day orbit of its parent star. That's 10 times quicker than the orbit of Mercury around the sun and means this blisteringly hot planet is classed as a " hot Jupiter ." However, something strange happened started to happen as astronomers observed the distant world. The orbits of the planet weren't regular like those of other planets, with TOI-2535 b often arriving six hours early or six hours later than when astronomers expected. Then, in March this year, TESS was no longer spotting the characteristic drops in starlight that TOI-2535 b caused as it crossed, or "transited," the face of its parent star. It seemed to have vanished. This team used TESS data to determine that TOI-2535 b is being pulled on by an unseen neighbor and is, in turn, pulling on that planet as well. This is causing the orbits of both worlds in the TOI-2535 system to "wobble." TOI-2535 b disappeared when that wobble tilted it out of alignment with its star. "We think of the universe as resembling clockwork, where everything is regular, but that's not true. If there are multiple planets in a system, they can affect each other's orbits. We know of a few systems that are like this," team member Samuel Yee of the University of California, Los Angeles, said in a statement . "This is the most extreme example we've seen because the two planets are interacting so strongly. The planet's orbit is tilting so quickly that its transit disappeared while we were watching." TOI-2535 b isn't expected to transit its parent star for at least 30 years, but the hidden neighbor tugging on it may cross the face of the star sooner than that. In the meantime, scientists will attempt to decode what this extreme wobbling exoplanet system says about how it formed. Hot Jupiters should be cool customers There is currently a lot of speculation about how hot Jupiter planets like TOI-2535 b form. That is because current routes of planet formation suggest planets like this would need to form around a great deal of ice. Obviously, ice isn't likely to be abundant as close to a star as TOI-2535 b is currently. This means that hot Jupiters likely form far from their stars and then migrate inwards . There are two ways that this could happen. The planet could be excited into an elliptical orbit by violent events like a near-collision with another planetary object, and then interactions with the star pull the planet inwards.
